editorial.headline: Paper Retail Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity spans everyday paper, board and paper-based goods; it is nationally open to foreign investment but cannot be registered as PMA in Bali under the permanent moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47613 covers the retail sale of paper, cardboard and goods made from them. Its working catalogue is broad but coherent: HVS paper, tracing paper, kraft paper, thin and coloured papers, Manila and buffalo-skin board, fibreboard, wrapping paper, food and beverage packaging board, paper bags, coated paper and board, stationery paper, stencil sheets, carbon paper and duplicator paper. In plain terms, this is the retail trade of paper and board products used for writing, copying, wrapping, packaging and related everyday purposes.

The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That matters because the classification is not confined to a single commercial footprint: the record accommodates operations from micro through large scale. The scope remains retail throughout. Its centre of gravity is the sale of paper, cardboard and paper-based merchandise, rather than a claim about manufacturing, distribution or any wider activity that the record does not state.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA and carries a maximum foreign ownership allowance of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore read the national position as fully open on the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here. The legal source listed for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no smaller national foreign-share cap in this record to soften or qualify that conclusion.

Bali is the decisive exception for a PMA applicant. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is recorded in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, and that assessment places the activity within Bali’s moratorium introduced in May 2026. The provincial rule is island-wide and permanent for this purpose: the Bali status is blocked because of the risk class, not because the national foreign-ownership ceiling is anything less than 100%. The honest reading is therefore two-part: nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium.
